audits.title: 25 A Retrospective Audit of Heart Failure Care in Older Patients at Campbelltown Hospital, NSW, with Reference to the 2017 ACCF/AHA Guideline

cycle1.result: No patients received all therapeutic options recommended by the guideline; most received basic blood tests and imaging; compliance lower for echocardiography, iron replacement and angiotensin blockers.

audits.other_findings: Median age 77, 71% frail; older patients trended towards fewer advanced investigations and appropriate medications.
audits.citation: Hsu A, Verick D, Blackwell M, Hohenberg M. 25 A Retrospective Audit of Heart Failure Care in Older Patients at Campbelltown Hospital, NSW, with Reference to the 2017 ACCF/AHA Guideline. Age and Ageing. 2019;48(Supplement_4):iv6-iv8. doi:10.1093/ageing/afz164.25.

audits.title: 589 Medication Prescribing for Patients Undergoing Cardiac Surgery with Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) and Review of Left Ventricular (LV) Function Documentation - A Departmental Audit
audits.standard: 2016 ESC guidelines: ACEi/ARNI, beta-blocker and MRA prescribed, titrated or contraindication documented in HFrEF (LVEF 40% or less)
audits.setting: Cardiac surgery department, Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh
audits.other_findings: 217 patients screened; barriers were LVEF not available on ward rounds, lack of awareness and unclear responsibility. Interventions to communicate LVEF and heart failure clinic referral have been introduced before a next cycle.

audits.title: Variation in hospital performance for heart failure management in the National Heart Failure Audit for England and Wales.
audits.standard: Key performance measures: ACE inhibitor/ARB and beta-blocker on discharge and referral to specialist follow-up
audits.setting: 185 hospitals in England and Wales (National Heart Failure Audit)

cycle1.result: Hospital adherence to composite KPM ranged from 50% to 97% (median 79%); only 8% of variation was attributable to hospital features.

audits.other_findings: Specialist follow-up referral varied more (median 81%, range 20% to 100%), with 26% attributable to hospital differences.
audits.citation: Emdin CA, Conrad N, Kiran A, Salimi-Khorshidi G, Woodward M, Anderson SG, et al.. Variation in hospital performance for heart failure management in the National Heart Failure Audit for England and Wales. Heart. 2017;103(1):55-62. doi:10.1136/heartjnl-2016-309706. PMID: 27530132.

audits.title: Evaluation of demographic, clinical characteristics, and the prescribing practice of guideline-directed medical therapy among chronic heart failure outpatients in multidisciplinary clinics in a large tertiary hospital: a retrospective audit of 1186 patients from 12 years
audits.standard: Guideline-directed medical therapy for chronic heart failure
audits.setting: Two multidisciplinary heart failure outpatient clinics at a tertiary hospital

cycle1.result: Similar GDMT prescribing in both clinics for HFrEF; ACEI/ARB prescription in HFpEF 70.5% (pharmacist clinic) vs 56.2%; low β-blocker and MRA prescription in both clinics.

audits.other_findings: Digoxin in chronic AF higher in HFrEF at pharmacist clinic (82.5% v 58.5%); anticoagulation in AF lower in HFpEF at that clinic.

audits.setting: Rural and remote general practices, Queensland

cycle1.result: 30% not receiving adequate ACE inhibitor doses; 45% may benefit from a beta-blocker; 14% taking a drug that aggravates heart failure

audits.setting: 86 hospitals in England and Wales (national heart failure audit)

cycle1.result: Echocardiograms in 75%; at discharge >90% loop diuretics, 80% ACE inhibitors or ARBs, 50% beta-blockers, 30% aldosterone antagonists; natriuretic peptides rarely measured.

audits.title: Improving medication titration in heart failure by embedding a structured medication titration plan.
audits.standard: Evidence-based target doses of ACEI/ARB and beta-blockers in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
audits.setting: Three heart failure disease management services, Queensland

cycle1.result: 37% reached target ACEI/ARB dose and 38% target beta-blocker dose.

audits.intervention: Structured medication titration plan for hospital-to-primary-care communication, introduced with education, audit and feedback, integration into work practice and incentive payments.

cycle2.result: 55% reached target ACEI/ARB dose (p=0.051) and 51% target beta-blocker dose (p=0.045).

audits.other_findings: Intervention cohort B (n=95) achieved 48% ACEI/ARB and 33% beta-blocker targets; responsibility for titration shifted to primary care.
audits.citation: Hickey A, Suna J, Marquart L, Denaro C, Javorsky G, Munns A, et al.. Improving medication titration in heart failure by embedding a structured medication titration plan. Int J Cardiol. 2016;224:99-106. doi:10.1016/j.ijcard.2016.09.001. PMID: 27643473.

audits.title: Audit of a tertiary heart failure outpatient service to assess compliance with NICE guidelines.
audits.setting: Tertiary heart failure outpatient service, Royal Brompton Hospital, London

cycle1.result: LVSD patients: beta-blockers 77%, ACE inhibitor or ARB 86%, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist 44%.

cycle2.result: LVSD patients (n=434): beta-blockers 89%, ACE inhibitor or ARB 91%, MRA 56%, ivabradine 6%; all reviewed at least 6-monthly.

audits.other_findings: All patients educated about exercise but only 21 (4%) enrolled in supervised exercise; poor access to cardiac rehabilitation.

audits.standard: Australian National Heart Foundation chronic heart failure guidelines (evidence-based therapy at discharge)

cycle1.result: At discharge 52% on ACEI/ARB, 49% on beta-blockers, 15% on aldosterone antagonists, 90% on diuretics and 29% on digoxin.

audits.title: A physician targeted intervention improves prescribing in chronic heart failure in general medical units.
audits.standard: Prescription of beta-blockers and ACEI/ARB in chronic heart failure
audits.setting: General medical units, Northern Health, Epping
audits.intervention: Structured physician education programme (November 2009 to January 2011) followed by quarterly performance feedback to each unit from February 2011

cycle2.result: Beta-blocker prescription rose to 92% (p=0.003) then maintained at 89%; ACEI/ARB rose to 93% (p=0.028) with feedback.

audits.other_findings: 468 patients in total; 180-day CHF readmissions fell in line with prescribing improvements.
audits.citation: Chua CC, Hutchinson A, Tacey M, Parikh S, Lim WK, Aboltins C. A physician targeted intervention improves prescribing in chronic heart failure in general medical units. BMC Health Serv Res. 2018;18(1):206. doi:10.1186/s12913-018-3009-x. PMID: 29566753.

audits.title: An audit of Heart failure management among ambulatory adult patients at Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital (QECH), Malawi.
audits.standard: Guideline-directed medical therapy at recommended doses for heart failure
audits.setting: Adult chest clinic, Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital, Blantyre

cycle1.result: 77% (61/79) on ACEI, 52% (42/79) on beta blocker, 34% (27/79) on aldosterone antagonist; recommended doses achieved in 14% (9/61) ACEI, 24% (10/42) beta blocker, 22% (6/27) aldosterone antagonist.

audits.title: Impact of Clinical Audit on Adherence to the Guidelines Directed Medical Therapy in Patients Admitted with Heart Failure.
audits.standard: Guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

cycle1.result: Unreasonable omission of ACEI/ARB/ARNI 24.5%, beta-blockers 13.1%, MRA 9.09%; ivabradine started before beta-blocker optimisation in 38.18%.

audits.intervention: Monthly clinical pharmacist audit of discharge prescriptions with results and feedback presented to physicians.

cycle2.result: Unreasonable omissions reduced to nil (p=0.00); inappropriate ivabradine initiation reduced to nil.

audits.title: A Comparison of Prescribing Guideline-Advocated Treatment for Heart Failure at Discharge from Cardiology and Non-Cardiology Wards.
audits.standard: Heart failure management guidelines (guideline-advocated pharmacological and non-pharmacological treatment)
audits.setting: Cardiology and non-cardiology wards of a tertiary hospital (Fiona Stanley Hospital)

cycle1.result: Prescription of ACEI/ARB/ARNI and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists lower in non-cardiology vs cardiology wards (52% vs 80%).

audits.other_findings: Lower prescribing on non-cardiology wards appeared related to patient complexity rather than ward.
audits.citation: Dai L, Dorje T, Gootjes J, Shah A, Dembo L, Rankin J, et al.. A Comparison of Prescribing Guideline-Advocated Treatment for Heart Failure at Discharge from Cardiology and Non-Cardiology Wards. Heart Lung Circ. 2025;34(3):273-280. doi:10.1016/j.hlc.2024.11.019. PMID: 39939202.
